overview: Two mechanisms for nucleophilic substitution — one goes through a carbocation intermediate in two steps, the other happens in a single concerted step.
genZNote: This reaction is basically a reagent-and-substrate-based personality test.

aspects.label: Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Two-step: leaving group departs first, forming a carbocation intermediate, then the nucleophile attacks.
aspects.valueB: One concerted step: nucleophile attacks as the leaving group departs simultaneously (backside attack).

aspects.label: Rate Law
aspects.valueA: First-order — rate depends only on substrate concentration, Rate = k[substrate].
aspects.valueB: Second-order — rate depends on both substrate and nucleophile concentration, Rate = k[substrate][nucleophile].

aspects.label: Favored Substrate
aspects.valueA: Tertiary (stable carbocation) > secondary; primary is disfavored.
aspects.valueB: Primary (least steric hindrance) > secondary; tertiary is essentially blocked.

aspects.label: Stereochemistry Outcome
aspects.valueA: Racemization (attack possible from either face of the flat carbocation).
aspects.valueB: Inversion of configuration (backside attack forces a single stereochemical outcome).
